answerToSection28: Yes. Two normal V1 paths consume a value that only a projection made as a historical fact without evidence pertinent to it. (1) History, QE-R7ASE-01: when the athlete lifts a projected load, atDose promotes the stored start's whole dose, including its load ticks. When the projection ran two weeks ahead of history, the tick at the new load counts an exposure never executed. With identical ledgers, U holds tick 1 where the control holds tick 0, on a value marked rebuilt, and after a SHORT return the next load step comes one exposure early. (2) Planning, QE-R7ASE-02: the planner's D52 re-establishment threshold (calendar days from the last executed exposure) reads a projected last-performed date after the weekly reviews had the facts. 35 days after the last real exposure, the plan prescribes a known 22 kg never lifted, where the same facts reviewed prescribe the re-establishment by effort. QE-R7AB-01's own recorded path (P40 and variants) is closed.

findings.what: atDose (src/r6-adaptation.mjs:714-720) promotes {load, reps, loadTick} from the stored planning start when the deciding log equals the stored load. The load is evidenced; the tick is not. When the projection ran two weeks beyond history (a step, then an assumed exposure at the new load), the tick counts a missed session. Identical ledgers: U db-rdl/db-split-squat KNOWN24 tick 1 (basis WEEK_EVIDENCE week 8, rebuilt) against R6 tick 0. The only 24 kg exposure missed its target (3 of 5 reps) or had reps unlogged. After a SHORT return U steps to 26 kg on 2027-01-09, R6 on 2027-01-16. Identical at UTC, +9, -5, -10; the same numbers on the boundary copy through its old whole-start rule.
findings.reproduction: reviews/qe-r7ase-P51d-identical-ledgers.mjs (cell U against R6, identical ledgers); reviews/qe-r7ase-P51c-atdose-projected-tick-unmet.mjs (four time zones, BOUNDARY); reviews/qe-r7ase-P51b-atdose-projected-tick-dev.mjs
findings.stateAtom: strength exercise loadTick (db-rdl, db-split-squat): the count of successful exposures at the current load; by the same code also reps under a repetition-progression goal (inferred, not run). Recorded basis WEEK_EVIDENCE rebuilt; real provenance CONDITIONAL_PLAN week 7's assumption about week 6's missed Saturday
findings.fromGranularity: Yes. One strength exercise is one value (contract §3), and atDose promotes the value's dose tuple on the evidence of one atom (the load): a container-level promotion inside the value (I2, I5 at value scale)
findings.physicalSeparationNeeded: Not for this instance: promoting only the load and re-deriving the tick from executed exposures would close it in the current model. The pattern argues for it, though. History is reconstructed by copying values out of the planning record under per-value rules, and QE-R7AB-01 and this finding are two such copy rules, the second introduced by the fix. A HistoricalState advanced only by executed evidence removes the class structurally. That is the engineering recommendation for the Founder's decision

findings.what: The planner's D52 predicate needsReestablishment (src/r6-program.mjs:335, used at :362: 'in calendar days from its last executed exposure', note 'as of the last review') reads lastPerformed from the planning start. A weekly review updates lastPerformed only for an exercise performed that week, so a planned date carried from an unreviewed week survives every later review in which the exercise is missed. In P40's U: planning lastPerformed 2026-11-21 (never executed), history 2026-11-14, and projectedBase names both exercises. On 2026-12-19 (35 days after the last exposure) U prescribes db-rdl 3x5@3 KNOWN22 and db-split-squat 2x6@3 KNOWN22, never lifted; R prescribes the D52 REESTABLISH by effort. Identical at four time zones and on the boundary copy (planning unchanged). Same class: P52, return-step doses planned from a projected return step after the re-entry session was missed (U db-bench-press 2x6@3 RETURN_STEP, goblet-squat 2x5@3 FIRST_ESTABLISH; control 1x6@4 RETURN_ENTRY).
findings.reproduction: reviews/qe-r7ase-P50-reestablish-projected-date.mjs (cells U against R; four time zones; BOUNDARY); reviews/qe-r7ase-I02-same-facts.mjs (same facts); reviews/qe-r7ase-P52-fresh-exercise-entryweek.mjs (return steps)
findings.stateAtom: strength exercise lastPerformed in the planning view (stateTrace[k].strength.exercises[id].lastPerformed), read as the last executed exposure by needsReestablishment; in P52 the exercises' returnStep, read by the row's exposure kind
findings.fromGranularity: No. The value is correctly identified (projectedBase) and history is right. The planner evaluates a predicate defined on executed history against the planning view (contract E1 too broad)
findings.physicalSeparationNeeded: Separate read paths are needed: history-defined predicates inside the planner must read the historical view. Physical separation is one way to enforce it, not the only one. One record serving both views is what lets such a predicate silently read a projected atom

findings.what: E2: a run value read through an unreviewed week is not re-gated, so it can be ahead of its reviewed control. B's run is rebuilt (projectedBase: true), yet long is 70 against R's 65; only 65-minute long runs were executed. The 70 is week 2's evidence start (week 1's review stepped the executed 65); R's review of week 2 applies the cap-trim rule ('continues from what was prescribed', 65). A review's step, never a projection's: not §28's class. For the SSCTR: a SHORT return resumes a 70-minute long run never executed.

Cross-exercise: in a reviewed start a fresh exercise is held and takes the stored value. The planning review set it up with the planning view's entryWeek (the projected return steps of other exercises), and ruleOn also passes entryWeek: st.strength.entryWeek from the stored start. In P44's history, B's goblet-squat in U is established outside the return; in R it is at return step 1. U's atoms match the row executed (2x5@3 FIRST_ESTABLISH), so no unexecuted value enters. It is a dependence on another exercise's projected state (Founder §12, family E).

observations: QE-R7AB-02's class also shows U ahead in one atom (P40b cells 8-9, reviews/qe-r7ase-scratch-p40b-reps.mjs). An exactly executed strength week verifies the projection, which keeps the earlier rep target (7), where the review adopts the logged repetitions (6). It is an earlier historical value, not a projection. probes/COMPARE_R7ASE_NAMED.json's P40b note ('every remaining difference has U behind R') omits it.

Interpretation for the Founder: after a review steps a load from evidence (20 kg x target met -> 22), the runtime's historical load is the evidence-gated next load (e.g. P40b cell R saturdayLift/nothing: db-calf-raise 22 kg never lifted). This matches contract §4 and every earlier control. Founder §3 calls 'next prescribed load = 22 kg' projected; if historical load must mean the last load lifted, the load atom conflates two meanings.

Author's evidence coverage gaps: atDose is tested only with the projection one week ahead (stored tick 0); no mutant promotes a projected tick at the new load; the consumer audit's E1 rationale ('the next review reads the facts') was not tested against an atom a review does not move.
